title: Getting to know Datastar: hypermedia with signals
excerpt: A short intro to signals, SSE, and element patching.
body:
Datastar combines two ideas: signals on the client and SSE from the server.

A signal is a small piece of reactive state that lives in a data-signals attribute. The server can push HTML fragments at any time over SSE, and Datastar morphs the existing DOM so input focus and scroll position are preserved.

Why hypermedia?

There is no duplicate state on the client. The source of truth stays on the server; the client only renders.

title: SSE in native PHP without a framework
excerpt: Writing a clean event-stream with flush and dropped-connection detection.
body:
Server-Sent Events are just an HTTP response with Content-Type: text/event-stream that is never closed.

The key: disable buffering, send data: followed by a blank line, then flush(). Detect a dropped connection with connection_aborted() so the loop stops.

title: Flat-file JSON as a prototype database
excerpt: When JSON is enough, and how to write it safely.
body:
For small-to-medium content sites, JSON files are plenty: easy to read, easy to diff in Git, and zero configuration.

Write with LOCK_EX to stay safe under concurrent writes, and store with JSON_PRETTY_PRINT to keep it review-friendly.
